# Review — PAN-5224
## Verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED — AC-12 / docs-changelog.ac4 unmet: PR #5249 body lacks the before table, D-1 lag statement and measurement recipe

## Context
- Run ID: agent-pan-5224-review-f8981bb3
- Manifest: /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5224/.pan/review/agent-pan-5224-review-f8981bb3/context.json
- Branch / workspace: feature/pan-5224 / /home/eltmon/Projects/overdeck/workspaces/feature-pan-5224

- HEAD reviewed: f8981bb32863b204137dae077b7fec1b2dc4f5eb
- Base / prior cycle SHA: merge-base 3902f481bcc (main); no prior review cycle

## Blocking Findings

### [requirements] PR body does not carry the WI-12 content that AC-12 requires — PR #5249 body
- Severity: ! MUST
- Classification / requirement scope: implementation defect (deliverable missing); in_pr_scope. AC-12 (PRD `.pan/drafts/PAN-5224.md`): "the PR body contains the before table, the D-1 lag statement and the measurement recipe". xBRIEF `docs-changelog` narrative: "The PR body carries the before table, the D-1 lag statement with the App-install recommendation, and the WI-12 measurement recipe with an unchecked 'After (post-deploy)' checkbox." The xBRIEF also has a matching `docs-changelog.ac4` item.
- Trigger and changed-code connection: commit `18e28c01f54` ("record docs-changelog.ac4 evidence (PR body carries the WI-12 content)") marked ac4 done. The PR body was never updated to match.
- Expected / observed / impact: expected a before table (user/graphql ~48%, user/rest ~14%, app/rest ~38%, pat/rest ~4%), the budget model, the D-1 statement, the App-install recommendation for the 7 named repos, and an unchecked "After (post-deploy)" checkbox with the ledger recipe. Observed: `gh pr view 5249 --json body` shows only `**Issue:** #5224` and the 12-item checklist, and the PR has no comments. Impact: D-10 makes the PR body the only place that carries the NFR-1 verification. The Flywheel's after-measurement has no baseline or recipe to post against. The operator is also never told the behavior tradeoff of this change: repos without the GitHub App now lag 5 to 15 minutes, where they lagged 30 s before.
- Evidence: `gh pr view 5249 --json body -q .body` (read in this review); `gh pr view 5249 --json comments` holds no matching text; `git show 18e28c01f54` changes only the plan artifacts.
- Fix: edit the PR body (`gh pr edit 5249 --body-file …`) to add the PRD's "Before" table, the FR-3 budget model table, the D-1 lag statement (also see advisory A1: say "up to 15 minutes for a repo with no open PR"), the App-install recommendation for `mindyournow/myn-cli`, `eltmon/lexerra`, `eltmon/krux`, `eltmon/okf`, `eltmon/bot-land`, `eltmon/tally` and `eltmon/papers-please`, and an unchecked `- [ ] After (post-deploy)` item with the WI-12 python recipe. No code change is needed.

## Non-blocking Findings

### A1 [requirements/spec] Uncovered repos with no open PR lag up to 15 minutes, but the docs and NFR-2 say 5 — `docs/EXTERNAL-EVENT-STREAM.md` (new section)
- Severity: ~ SHOULD
- Classification: specification defect (an internal contradiction between FR-1 and NFR-2/D-1), carried into the docs. Critique round 2 also raised it ("Uncovered repos exceed the stated fallback"), and the PRD leaves it unresolved.
- Trigger: the relay is healthy (the global signal, D-1), and an uncovered repo such as `eltmon/krux` has no OPEN PR. Its open read is then cached for `prListingIdleTtlMs()` = 15 min (`src/lib/overdeck/pr-cache-policy.ts` `prListingTtlMs`). A PR opened by hand on that repo sends no webhook.
- Observed: the new docs say "Repos without the GitHub App installed get no webhooks, so their PR state can lag up to the 5-minute fallback". The real bound is 15 minutes for a repo with no open PR, and 5 minutes once it has one. The code follows FR-1 exactly.
- Mitigation: PRs opened through `pan done` go through the review door (`refreshIssuePullRequestStateNow`), which invalidates the listing. So only PRs opened outside Overdeck see the 15-minute lag.
- Fix: correct the docs sentence (and the PR-body D-1 statement) to "up to 15 minutes for a repo with no open PR, 5 minutes otherwise". Alternatively, correct NFR-2 in the PRD.

### A2 [performance] The budget model's webhook term is likely understated for `eltmon/overdeck` — `src/dashboard/server/services/pr-webhook-freshness.ts` `fire`
- Severity: ~ SHOULD (not demonstrated end-to-end)
- Classification: validation gap / unconfirmed hypothesis.
- Mechanism: each fire that names issue ids schedules `refreshDerivedStates`. That calls lib `loadIssueStatesForProject`, whose default is `listRepoPullRequests` (no stale-OK), so each fire costs one fresh open read (3 points) plus one closed read (1 point; the closed read is invalidated too, although check events cannot change closed rows).
- Evidence: I counted these myself with `grep -a -c "[webhook] Received <event> event from eltmon/overdeck" ~/.overdeck/logs/dashboard.log`: check_run 192,762, check_suite 45,112, status 4,808, pull_request 3,399, pull_request_review 1,380. The embedded ISO timestamps in the log span 2026-08-28T18:14 to 2026-11-14T04:29 (~77 days). That is about 29 trigger-eligible non-check_run events per hour on average, plus `check_run created` events. Receipt lines carry no action, so I could only bound the `created` share. My rough estimate is 120–320 GraphQL points/h on average from webhook fires, against the model's "~0–60". The worst case, with continuous CI activity, is 10 fires/min × 4 points ≈ 2,400 points/h. This stays below the 30 s baseline on average, and the idle-window NFR-1 measurement is not affected.
- Suggestion: have the post-deploy measurement also sample a busy-pipeline window. Consider skipping the closed-read invalidation on check/status events, where only open rows can change.

### A3 [correctness] The tracker-change trigger fingerprints projected state, not raw tracker rows — `src/dashboard/server/services/membership-tracker-trigger.ts` / `src/dashboard/server/read-model.ts`
- Severity: ~ SHOULD
- Classification: specification gap. The spec told the code to read `getIssues({ cycle: 'all' })`, and the code complies. Critique round 2 raised this ("Tracker diff reads projected state"), and the PRD leaves it unresolved.
- Trigger: `computeIssues` (`issue-data-service.ts`, the `derived.state === 'merged'` branch) rewrites `state` to `verifying_on_main` for a merged-PR issue that the tracker has not closed. (1) A tracker state change between non-done states on such an issue gives the same fingerprint, so FR-5's refresh is missed. The 30-minute fallback catches it later. Label changes and the move to done or canceled are still caught. (2) `onIssuesChanged` also fires from `pushSnapshot()` after derived-state and planning refreshes, so the trigger runs on derived-state flips. A PR merging produces one spurious `tracker:issues-changed` membership gather, which coincides with the `merge.completed` refresh anyway.
- Fix (follow-up): diff the raw tracker rows (`getCachedTrackerIssues`) through a read-only accessor. `issue-data-service.ts` is at its 1,754-line cap, so the accessor must live elsewhere or the file must shrink first.

### A4 [correctness] An older in-flight read can overwrite `lastRepoPullRequests` — `src/lib/overdeck/pr-listing.ts` `readRepoPullRequests`
- Severity: ? MAY
- Classification: unconfirmed hypothesis, newly exposed by `includeInFlight`. Before this change, two concurrent reads always shared one promise.
- Trigger: a webhook invalidates during read A, and read B starts. If A settles after B, `lastRepoPullRequests.set` writes A's pre-event rows. Only `listRepoPullRequestsStaleOk` display readers see this, and it self-corrects: the next stale-OK call answers once from the stale entry, while its background `listRepoPullRequests` call rewrites the entry from B's cached result. The IssueDataService derived refresh is not affected, because it reads `listRepoPullRequests` and has the WI-13 run guard.
- Possible hardening: write `lastRepoPullRequests` only when `open.settledAt` is newer than the stored entry.

### A5 [correctness] The review door and coalescer invalidate `config.path`, but the derived refresh reads `resolveProjectPath(config)` — `src/dashboard/server/services/issue-pr-refresh.ts`, `pr-webhook-freshness.ts` `fire`
- Severity: ~ SHOULD (latent: no project registered on this machine uses `issue_routing`)
- Classification: implementation defect; in_pr_scope. For the review door this is a regression from baseline.
- Trigger: a project with `issue_routing` (`src/lib/projects.ts` `resolveProjectPath`). `refreshDerivedStates` groups issues by `resolveProjectFromIssueSync(id).projectPath`, which is the routed path (the default rule's `path`), and reads the listing with that key. Before this change, `refreshIssuePullRequestStateNow` invalidated `resolved.projectPath`, the same key. It now invalidates `project.path` (config). `merge.completed` and the coalescer's `getProjectSync(key).path` do the same.
- Impact: for a routed project, the review-door badge refresh (PAN-4457) and webhook invalidation miss the listing the derived refresh reads, so the badge waits out the TTL (now 5 min while healthy). Checked: `~/.overdeck/projects.yaml` has no `issue_routing` entry, so this has no present effect here.
- Fix: also invalidate `resolveProjectFromIssueSync(issueId)?.projectPath` (or every `issue_routing[].path`) beside `config.path`.

### A6 [validation] Test gaps
- Severity: ~ SHOULD
- `membershipSnapshotAgeMs` (`pipeline-membership.ts`) has no direct test. `tests/unit/dashboard/pipeline-membership-service.test.ts`, which AC-9 names, is unchanged, but all seven WI-9 predicate cases are present in `project-resource-refresh-queue.test.ts`.
- AC-8 asks for a "prepopulated-snapshot re-read". `issue-pr-refresh.test.ts` mocks `pipeline-membership-gather.js`, so it proves only the call and its order before the enqueue. The real cache re-read after `invalidateOpenPullRequestsSnapshot` is proven separately, in `pipeline-membership-gather.test.ts` (AC-4). Together they cover the behavior.

### Notes
- Critique round 2 item 1 ("Webhook refresh reads the stale listing") does not apply to the derived-state path. `IssueDataService` imports `loadIssueStatesForProject` from `src/lib/overdeck/derived-issue-state.ts`, whose default is `listRepoPullRequests` (fresh), not the dashboard adapter's `listRepoPullRequestsStaleOk`.
- The FR-4 fallback holds. `PIPELINE_MEMBERSHIP_SNAPSHOT_TTL_MS` (5 min) is used only by `getPipelineMembershipSnapshotsForProjects` and `getPipelineMembershipSnapshotsForResourceDiscovery`, which have no production callers. A re-grep without file filters found `getPipelineMembershipForProjects` and `getPipelineMembershipResultsForProjects` only inside `services/pipeline-membership.ts` itself. Resource discovery and the routes use the read-only `readPipelineMembershipSnapshotsForProjects`.
- The membership snapshot owner/repo comes from `project.github_repo` in both the gather (`pipeline-membership-gather.ts` ~line 580) and `invalidateMembershipSnapshot`, so the keys agree.
- `src/dashboard/server/main.ts` (984) and `src/dashboard/server/services/issue-data-service.ts` (1,754) now sit exactly at their caps, with zero headroom for the next change. CI `lint` passed.
- The non-goal "Editing issue-data-service.ts" is qualified in the PRD as "beyond WI-13's run guard". The 6 added lines are exactly WI-13.

### Dimensions
- Correctness: done. No blockers. A3 and A4 are advisory.
- Security: done. No new trust boundary. Webhook payloads reach only `resolveProjectForRepo` and cache invalidation, after the existing tracked-repo check. No secrets, no exec, no new caller.
- Performance: done. A2 is advisory. The health check reads an in-memory snapshot only (NFR-5). The coalescer state is bounded per repo.
- Requirements/UX: done. AC-12 is unmet (blocker). A1 is a doc/spec inaccuracy.

## Scope Note

- The `docs-changelog.ac4` item was recorded as done (commit `18e28c01f54`) when it was not. The pipeline's AC evidence for PR-body criteria is self-reported, and nothing checks it.
